A safe overview:
SQL injection happens when an app mixes untrusted input into SQL queries, letting input change the query’s meaning. Common causes are string concatenation in queries, poor input handling, verbose database errors, and over-privileged database accounts.
The main defenses are:
use parameterized queries / prepared statements everywhere
avoid dynamic SQL where possible
validate and constrain input by type, length, and allowed values
use least-privilege database credentials
suppress detailed DB errors from users and log them securely
add monitoring, WAF rules, and security tests in CI
A safe testing workflow for your own systems:
Inventory all inputs that reach the database.
Review code for concatenated SQL.
Replace risky queries with parameterized ones.
Run authorized scans with tools configured for defensive testing.
Add unit/integration tests for common injection cases.
Confirm least-privilege DB permissions and rotate secrets.
Monitor logs for suspicious query patterns.
